intro: You are entering Istanbul Archaeological Museums, in İstanbul province: Türkiye's first museum, founded in 1891 by Osman Hamdi Bey. Here the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Kadesh treaty tablet and the Tiled Kiosk share a single garden. Where shall we start?
history: Osman Hamdi Bey opened the museum in 1891, and its birth was tied to a turning point: the regulations that stopped antiquities leaving the Ottoman Empire. What came out of the ground needed somewhere to stay, and this became that place. Today it has three parts: the Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient and the Tiled Kiosk. At the heart of the collection lie the sarcophagi from the royal necropolis of Sidon.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Alexander Sarcophagus and the Sarcophagus of the Mourning Women. Look for the Kadesh treaty tablet and the Ishtar Gate panels, and then step across to the Tiled Kiosk.
facts: Did you know? The Alexander Sarcophagus is misnamed. It was made not for Alexander but for Abdalonymus, king of Sidon in his time; Alexander appears only in the carving. This was also Türkiye's first museum, born alongside the rules that stopped antiquities leaving the country, because what came out of the ground needed somewhere to stay. And one more treasure: the cuneiform tablet of the Treaty of Kadesh is here, while a copy of this oldest known written peace treaty hangs at the UN in New York.
outro: This brings our tour of Istanbul Archaeological Museums to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these treasures stay safe for the visitors who follow. Enjoy the rest of your visit.
